agyos_skill.intent: Master rule for skill usage. Prevents rationalization and enforces strict adherence to all existing skills. Triggers on any task, question, or action.
agyos_skill.instructions: **If there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to your task, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke and follow the skill BEFORE taking action.** This is not negotiable. This is not optional. You cannot rationalize your way out of this. ALWAYS. Use this mindset at the beginning of every conversation, task, or question. When processing a user request, sequence your skills: 1. **Planning/Process Skills First:** (e.g., `brainstorming-designs.md`, `qa-tdd-architect.md`). These dictate HOW you approach the problem. 2. **Architecture Skills Second:** (e.g., `architecture-python-backend.md`, `architecture-frontend-design.md`, `architecture-database-design.md`). These protect the structure. 3. **Tech-Stack Skills Third:** (e.g., `fastapi-backend-patterns.md`, `nextjs-heroui-frontend.md`). These provide the exact implementation details. If you think any of the following, STOP and load the relevant skill: - ❌ *"This is just a simple code change."* (Simple things break. Use TDD/QA skills.) - ❌ *"I'll just fix this one bug first, then look at the skill."* (Use the systematic debugging skill BEFORE touching code.) - ❌ *"I know how React works, I don't need to read the guideline."* (Knowing the concept ≠ using the specific project guidelines.) - ❌ *"I'll verify it manually."* (Ad-hoc testing is forbidden. Use TDD.) At every step (Gate 4), ensure you have: 1. **PRE-ACT:** Read the relevant skill checklist. 2. **ACT:** Implemented exactly according to the skill. 3. **VERIFY:** Tested against the skill's criteria.
